To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a submicron-scale architecture of beta-TCP induces substantial bone formation, is remodeled at an equivalent rate and is populated by osteoclast-like cell.
submicron-scale TCP surface architecture induces bone formation and resorption in vitro and in a rat muscle pouch model.
the submicron-scale architecture of tricalcalcium phosphate (beta-TCP) directs osteoclast differentiation and activity in vitro and in intramuscular implants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the engineering of bone graft substitutes that can be used for the repair of skeletal defects.
the design and fabrication of synthetic bone substitutes with the capacity to induce bone formation and resorption.
the development of synthetic bone graft substitutes that are osteoinductive and resorbable at a rate similar to that of bone, and that may therefore be useful in the treatment of bone defects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
submicron surface architecture of tracalcium phosphate induces osteogenesis in vitro, and in vivo, and is resorped at an equivalent rate.
submicron-architecture of beta-TCP induces osteogenesis and is resorped by osteoclasts in vitro and in vitro.
the submicron surface architecture of beta-TCP directs osteogenesis in vivo by inducing osteoclast differentiation and activation, which is essential for both bone formation and resorption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface architecture of synthetic bone substitutes can direct osteogenesis in vitro as well as in vivo.
the surface structure of TCP is a key determinant of bone formation in vivo and that the submicron-scale architecture of TCP is a promising design for bone graft substitutes.
submicron-scale TCP is a bone graft substitute that is resorbed and induces bone formation at similar rates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface architecture of a synthetic bone graft can be engineered to induce bone formation and to control resorption.
the submicron-scale structure of TCP can direct osteogenesis, which may provide a new approach towards designing synthetic bone grafts with osteogenic and resorptive capacity.
the surface architecture of a synthetic bone graft substitute is a crucial determinant of its osteoinductive and resorption properties.
